target: Eu assistiria ao filme de novo com prazer.
english: I would watch the movie again with pleasure.
tip: The verb assistir takes a when it means 'to watch', so it is assistir ao filme, not assistir o filme.

target: A razão pela qual ele faltou é desconhecida.
english: The reason why he was absent is unknown.
tip: pela qual is por plus a qual, literally 'by which'; Portuguese says a razão pela qual for 'the reason why'.

target: O programa que assistimos ontem foi muito informativo.
english: The program we attended yesterday was very informative.
tip: Programa is masculine even though it ends in -a: o programa que assistimos.

target: Nós iríamos à praia, mas está chovendo.
english: We would go to the beach, but it's raining.
tip: The crase joins a plus a into à before a feminine noun: nós iríamos à praia.

target: Eu vou pensar no assunto.
english: I'll think about it.
tip: The verb pensar takes em, not de, and em + o becomes no: pensar no assunto = think about the matter.

target: Quem não arrisca não petisca.
english: Nothing ventured, nothing gained.
tip: A common Brazilian proverb using 'quem' – 'whoever doesn't risk, doesn't snack'.

target: Eu nunca esquecerei esse momento.
english: I'll never forget this moment.
tip: With nunca before the verb, no second negative is needed: nunca esquecerei = I will never forget.

target: Ela vai fazer aniversário semana que vem.
english: She's having her birthday next week.
tip: Fazer aniversário, literally to make a birthday, is the set phrase for having one: vai fazer aniversário.

target: Eles vão se mudar para Curitiba.
english: They're going to move to Curitiba.
tip: Plain mudar means change; the reflexive se mudar means to relocate: vão se mudar para Curitiba.

target: Ela tinha cozinhado um jantar especial.
english: She had cooked a special dinner.
tip: Tinha plus a past participle is the pluperfect, an action done before another past moment: tinha cozinhado = had cooked.

target: Você vai ver, vai dar tudo certo.
english: You'll see, everything will work out.
tip: Dar certo is the fixed phrase for to work out or turn out fine: vai dar tudo certo = it'll all work out.

target: Haverá uma festa de confraternização na empresa.
english: There will be a company party.
tip: Haverá is the formal 'there will be'; everyday speech would say vai ter uma festa instead.

target: Vocês vão ter que esperar um pouco.
english: You'll have to wait a bit.
tip: Ter que plus an infinitive expresses obligation: vão ter que esperar = you'll have to wait.

target: Ela tinha pintado o quarto de branco.
english: She had painted the room white.
tip: To name the color something is painted, use de plus the color: pintado o quarto de branco = painted it white.

target: Nós tínhamos escolhido o restaurante com cuidado.
english: We had chosen the restaurant carefully.
tip: Com plus a noun often replaces an -mente adverb: com cuidado = carefully, literally with care.

target: Ela já tinha ligado para o médico.
english: She had already called the doctor.
tip: Ligar meaning to phone someone takes para: tinha ligado para o médico = had called the doctor.

target: A gente vai comemorar no fim de semana.
english: We're going to celebrate this weekend.
tip: A gente means we but takes a singular verb: a gente vai, never a gente vão.

target: O momento em que ele chegou, todos aplaudiram.
english: The moment he arrived, everyone applauded.
tip: For a point in time the relative is em que, not bare que: o momento em que ele chegou = the moment when.

target: Nós iremos ao evento juntos.
english: We will go to the event together.
tip: The preposition a plus o contracts to ao: iremos ao evento = we will go to the event.

target: Eu vou me inscrever no concurso.
english: I'm going to register for the exam.
tip: In Brazilian Portuguese the pronoun goes before the infinitive: vou me inscrever, not vou inscrever-me.

target: Eu vou esperar até ela chegar.
english: I'm going to wait until she arrives.
tip: After até, Portuguese uses an infinitive that names its own subject: até ela chegar = until she arrives.

target: Eu direi a verdade quando for necessário.
english: I'll tell the truth when it's necessary.
tip: For a future condition after quando, use the future subjunctive: quando for necessário = when it is necessary.

target: Será que ele vai aceitar o convite?
english: Do you think he'll accept the invitation?
tip: Será que opens a speculative question, like I wonder if or do you think: Será que ele vai aceitar?

target: A pessoa de quem eu gosto mora longe.
english: The person I like lives far away.
tip: In formal Portuguese, 'de quem' is used with verbs requiring 'de': gostar de.

target: A estrada pela qual passamos estava em obras.
english: The road we traveled along was under construction.
tip: After a preposition use a qual or o qual: por plus a qual becomes pela qual = along which.

target: Vocês vão participar do churrasco?
english: Are you going to come to the barbecue?
tip: Participar takes de, and de + o becomes do: participar do churrasco = take part in the barbecue.

target: Vocês vão ficar aqui ou vão embora?
english: Are you going to stay here or leave?
tip: Ir embora, not just ir, means to leave; embora is required: vão embora = they go away.

target: O museu onde vimos aquela exposição reabriu.
english: The museum where we saw that exhibition reopened.
tip: Onde means where and refers only to places: o museu onde vimos = the museum where we saw.

target: Eu tenho dormido mal nas últimas semanas.
english: I've been sleeping badly the past few weeks.
tip: Tenho plus a participle isn't a one-time past; it means ongoing and repeated lately: tenho dormido mal = I've been sleeping badly.

target: Se ela falasse mais devagar, todos entenderiam.
english: If she spoke more slowly, everyone would understand.
tip: For -ar verbs the imperfect subjunctive ends in -asse: falar becomes falasse, as in Se ela falasse = if she spoke.
